title: Hotel booking and double bookings
idea: A hotel booking design stores bookings as date ranges per room, and makes the overlap check and the save one step, so no night is sold twice.
points: A stay is a half-open range `[from, to)`; checkout day stays free.
Two ranges clash when each one starts before the other ends.
Checking then saving with an `await` between them lets a second request slip in.

hero.title: Two guests, one room, one night

items.label: Ann reads
items.text: Ann's request reads room 101's bookings. There are none, so her check passes.

items.label: Bo reads
items.text: Before Ann's save lands, Bo reads the same empty list. His check passes too.

items.label: Both save
items.text: Ann's booking is written, then Bo's. Night 4 now has two guests.

items.label: Add a lock
items.text: A per-room lock queues Bo's check-and-save behind Ann's. Other rooms carry on.

items.label: Bo runs next
items.text: Bo's queued check runs after Ann's save. He sees her booking and is refused.

code.title: Race, then lock
code.caption: The repository fakes a database with a timer. Three guests ask for room 101 at once, first without a lock, then with one.

walk.text: Each repository call waits a tick, like a real database round trip.
Half-open ranges: a stay ending on day 5 does not clash with one starting on 5.
`KeyedLock` chains tasks per key, so tasks for one room run one at a time.
The check and the save form one task: the critical section.
Without a lock the task runs at once and can interleave with others.
Ann and Bo overlap on night 4. Cy starts on Ann's checkout day.

pitfalls: Never check availability and save in separate steps with an `await` between them.
An in-memory lock covers one process only; with several servers use a database constraint.
Store stays as `[from, to)`; inclusive end dates make back-to-back stays clash.

quiz.why: The first pair only touch on day 5, and `5 < 5` is false. The second range sits inside the first, so both comparisons hold.

takeaway: Overlap check and save must be one atomic step per room.

starters: How would a database unique or exclusion constraint prevent double booking?
Should I use optimistic or pessimistic locking for hotel rooms?
How do I search for any free room of a given type?
